verdicts.quote: “External applications… need to handle the oAuth process… These apps use oAuth2 flow to get access token for a specific Ecwid store.”
verdicts.reason: Vendor authentication docs explicitly state OAuth2 for public/external apps, which is what a multi-tenant agent would use.

verdicts.quote: “Only stores on paid plans can access API.”
verdicts.reason: Confirms API access is gated to paid plans (even though they may grant a free dev upgrade on request).

verdicts.quote: “Ecwid REST API allows you to access and manage any store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings.”
verdicts.reason: The overview plus the extensive endpoint list across products, orders, customers, categories, discounts, settings indicates broad coverage.

verdicts.quote: “Access Ecwid API Platform … REST API, Webhooks, Payment and Shipping methods and others, are done by applications.”
verdicts.reason: I found no mention of an official Ecwid MCP server in Ecwid’s docs/site/GitHub as of Nov 24, 2026; only third‑party MCP servers appear elsewhere, which don’t count as “official.” Cannot confirm “none” from a primary source.

verdicts.quote: “There is no test mode in Ecwid API, so we recommend setting up a separate test store.”
verdicts.reason: Buildable today (self-serve dev app/tokens), but caveats include paid-plan requirement for API access and no sandbox/test mode; public OAuth apps also undergo validation before App Market release.
